This template summarizes information about a piece of [[legislation]] or a [[:en:Bill (law)|bill]]. It is designed to be generic so that it can be used for the bills, [[:en:Statute|Statute]]s and subsidiary legislation ([[delegated legislation]]) of any [[:en:Jurisdiction|Jurisdiction]]. If you have suggestions as to how the template may be improved, please leave a message on the [[Template talk:Infobox legislation|talk page]].

Specific infoboxes for European Union, United Kingdom (national and devolved) and United States (federal only) legislation are at {{tl|Infobox EU legislation}}, {{tl|Infobox UK legislation}} and {{tl|Infobox U.S. legislation}} respectively (although this template also supports the latter two to a limited extent).

===Legislation enacted by a legislature (e.g. an Act of Parliament/Congress)===
See next section for bills that did not pass or is still being considered by the legislature.

==Parameters==
This infobox takes a number of parameters, which are all optional:

{|class="wikitable"
|-
!Parameter
!Description
|-
|colspan="2" bgcolor="silver"|'''Basic information'''
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''short_title'''
|The [[:en:Short title|Short title]] of the legislation or bill, which should preferably be the same as the article title. If the parameter is left blank or omitted, the article name is used.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''legislature'''
|The name of the [[:en:Legislature|Legislature]] that enacted the legislation. You only need to use this parameter if the legislature of the jurisdiction in question is [[:en:Bicameralism|bicameral]], and you wish to state its name rather than just the names of the [[:en:upper house|upper house]] and [[:en:lower house|lower house]], which can be specified using {{para|enacted_by}} and {{para|enacted_by2}}.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''image'''
|An image which represents the legislation's topic or enactment process. Type the name of the image without the "{{mono|File:}}" prefix and do not [[Help:Link|wikilink]] it.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''imagesize'''
|The width of the image in [[:en:Pixel|Pixel]]s (px), particularly if it is less than 180 px. Type the number without the "px" suffix ("{{mono|150}}", not "{{mono|150px}}"). If this parameter is left blank or omitted, the image size defaults to 180 px.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''image_upright'''
|Scale factor for the image, particularly to scale tall, narrow images correctly. See [[Help:Pictures#Upright_images]] for more information.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''imagealt'''
|[[Wikipedia:Extended image syntax#Alt text and caption|Alt text]] for the image. For more information, see "[[Wikipedia:Alternative text for images]]".
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''caption'''
|A caption for the image. Terms in the caption can be wikilinked, if desired.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''long_title'''
|The [[long title]] of the legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''citation'''
|The citation of the legislation. If the legislation is available online, use a [[:Category:Law citation templates|citation template]] where available to generate an external link automatically, or else [[Help:Link#External links|create a link manually]]. If the citation uses square brackets, replace them with {{mono|&amp;#91;}} and {{mono|&amp;#93;}} when putting them inside an external link.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''territorial_extent'''
|The territorial area(s) to which the legislation extends or applies. If possible, provide a wikilink.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''considered_by<br />enacted_by'''
|The name of the person or institution that considered or enacted the legislation. {{para|considered_by}} is used for proposed or failed legislation (e.g. bills) in which the institution did not or has not enacted the legislation, and {{para|enacted_by}} for successful ones. Wikilink the name to a Wikipedia article about the person or institution, if there is one. In a bicameral jurisdiction, use this parameter to specify the legislative chamber that initiated the legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_enacted<br />date_passed'''
|The date the legislation was enacted or passed. Select either {{para|date_enacted}} or {{para|date_passed}} depending on whether the term ''enacted'' or ''passed'' is customarily used in the jurisdiction. In line with "[[Wikipedia:Manual of Style (dates and numbers)#Linking and autoformatting of dates]]", do not wikilink dates.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''considered_by2<br />enacted_by2<br />date_enacted2<br />date_passed2'''
|In a bicameral legislature, use these parameters to specify the name of the legislative chamber that considered the legislation after it was initiated by the other chamber, and the date when the second chamber enacted or passed the legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_assented<br />royal_assent<br />date_signed'''
|Use one of the following:
#{{para|date_assented}} – to indicate the date when a [[:en:Head of state|Head of state]] or their representative gives formal assent to the legislation.
#{{para|royal_assent}} – to indicate the date when a [[:en:Constitutional monarchy|constitutional monarch]] gives [[royal assent]] to legislation.
#{{para|date_signed}} – to indicate the date when a [[:en:Head of state|Head of state]] or their representative in jurisdictions which do not use the term "assent" signs a piece of legislation (''e.g.'', the [[President of Ireland]]; the [[governor (United States)|governor of one of the US states]]; a [[:en:Constitutional monarchy|constitutional monarch]] without royal assent powers such, as the [[Grand Duke of Luxembourg]])

Do not use parameter(s) from two or three of the above categories together.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''assented_by<br />signed_by'''
|Use one of the following:
#{{para|assented_by}} – to indicate the assenter's identity where {{para|date_assented}} or {{para|royal_assent}} is used.
#{{para|signed_by}} – to indicate the signer's identity where {{para|date_signed}} is used.

Do not use parameter(s) from two of the above categories together. The official title should precede the full name (e.g. “President John Doe”, not “John Doe” or “President Doe”).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_vetoed'''
|The date when the legislation was [[vetoed]] by the [[:en:Head of state|Head of state]] or their representative. This does not apply to a [[pocket veto]].
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_type'''
|The type of veto applied to the law, if the [[:en:Head of state|Head of state]] or their representative has the right to veto the bill in multiple ways. This does not apply to a [[pocket veto]].

Use one of the following:
#Absolute – to indicate a veto which cannot be overridden (''e.g.'', withholding of royal assent by the [[Monarch of the United Kingdom]], or a final veto by the [[President of Cyprus]]).
#Package – to indicate a veto where the entire bill is returned to the legislature for reconsideration.
#Line-item – to indicate a veto where only a part of the bill is returned to the legislature for reconsideration.
#Reservation – to indicate a veto where the bill is submitted to the decision of a third party, other than a court or other authority with judicial review powers; typically, this would be the people in a referendum (''e.g.'', a reservation of the bill to the significance of the people by the [[President of Ireland]]), though submission to a non-judicial third authority exists as well (''e.g.'' [[Disallowance and reservation in Canada|reservation in Canada]]).
#Constitutional – to indicate a veto where the bill is referred to the supreme or constitutional court, or other authority with [[:en:Judicial review|Judicial review]] powers, to determine its constitutionality.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_overridden'''
|The date when the veto was [[veto override|overridden]]:
#If the veto involves returning the bill to the legislature, this is the date of the legislative vote to override the veto. If the legislative debates are available online, create external links to them.
#If the veto involves submitting the bill to a referendum, this is the date of the referendum on that bill. Create an internal link to that Referendum's article.
#If the veto involves submitting the bill to non-judicial third authority, this is the date that third authority overturned the veto.

This does not apply to a [[pocket veto]] or a constitutional veto.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''reference_holding'''
|The decision of the supreme or constitutional court, or other authority with [[:en:Judicial review|Judicial review]] powers, on a vetoed bill referred to it. Create an internal link to the court ruling's article; if no such article exists but the court's decision is available online, create an external link to it.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_pocket_vetoed'''
|The date when the legislation was [[pocket veto]]ed by the [[:en:Head of state|Head of state]] or their representative (''i.e.'' the bill became ineffective because the head of state or representative did not sign/assent or veto it within an allowed time).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_became_law_by_inaction'''
|The date when the legislation bill became law because the head of state or representative did not sign/assent or veto it within an allowed time.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_commenced'''<br />'''date_effective'''
|The date when the legislation commenced ([[:en:Coming into force|came into force]]), or [[effective date|became effective]] as law. Use the parameter that corresponds to the term customary in the jurisdiction, not both the parameters.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_of_expiry'''
|Date when the legislation automatically ceases to have effect (usually, but not always, when a [[Sunset clause|sunset provision]] is included).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_repealed'''
|Date when the legislation is repealed. Note that legislation may be repealed before or after it had expired, so this parameter is not necessarily identical to {{para|date_of_expiry}}.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_abrogated'''
|Date when the legislation is abrogated without a formal repeal by the legislature, such as being struck down as unconstitutional, disallowed, or abrogated in a [[popular referendum]].
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''administered_by'''
|The institution administering the legislation. Not necessary for most legislation. Wikilink if possible.
|-
|colspan="2" bgcolor="silver"|'''Legislative history'''
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''bill_history_url'''
|URL of the webpage on the legislature's website (or equivalent) that shows the legislative history of the bill, if available. Sometimes known as the "bill homepage".
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''bill'''
|The name of the [[:en:Bill (law)|bill]] or proposed law when the legislation was still being considered by the institution specified in {{para|enacted_by}} or {{para|considered_by}}. Wikilink the name to an article about the bill, if there is one.

In a bicameral jurisdiction, use this parameter to state the name of the bill that was introduced by the legislative chamber that initiated the legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''bill_citation'''
|The citation of the bill. If the bill is available online, create an external link to it. If the citation uses square brackets, replace them with {{mono|&amp;#91;}} and {{mono|&amp;#93;}} when putting them inside an external link.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''introduced_by'''
|The name of the legislator or other authority who introduced the bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''cosponsored_by'''
|The legislator(s) co-sponsoring the bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_introduced'''
|The date when the bill was introduced.

Do not use this parameter if the introduction is considered part of another stage (e.g. First readings in Commonwealth realms, which are typically just the introduction of the bill, instead of a debate on its general outlines followed by a vote on whether or not to send it to committee form of First reading common in non-Westminster legislatures).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_distributed'''
|The date when the bill was distributed for circulation among MPs.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''committee_responsible'''
|The name of the Committee responsible for the topic of the bill. Use only the name of the committee itself (for example, "[[United States House Committee on Financial Services|Financial Services]]" instead of "[[United States House Committee on Financial Services]]").
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''member_in_charge<br />rapporteur'''
|The name of the legislator responsible for handling the bill, if different from the person who introduced it. Use the parameter that corresponds to the term customary in the jurisdiction, not both the parameters.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading<br />1st_reading<br />2nd_reading<br />3rd_reading'''
|The dates of the [[reading (legislature)#Preliminary reading|preliminary]], [[reading (legislature)#First reading|first]], [[reading (legislature)#Second reading|second]] and [[reading (legislature)#Third reading|third readings]] of the bill in the legislature. If the legislative debates are available online, create external links to them.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''passed'''
|The date when the bill was finally passed by the chamber in jurisdictions that do not use numbered readings (e.g. Continental European legislatures).

Do not use this parameter together with the readings parameters.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''committee_post1st<br />committee_post2nd'''
|The date(s) when the bill was considered by a legislative committee (other than a committee of the whole) between readings. Use committee_post1st and committee_post2nd as appropriate in the jurisdiction - committee_post1st if it occurs between first and second readings (Israel, US House of Representatives), and committee_post2nd if it occurs between second and third readings (US Senate, UK, Australia), not both the parameters.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''committee_whole_label<br />committee_whole'''
|In some jurisdictions, name of the stage between the second and third readings where the bill is examined in detail (usually clause by clause), and the date(s) when it occurred. This is often named the "[[committee of the whole]]" (default), or sometimes the "committee stage" (Ireland, New Zealand) or "consideration in detail" (most lower houses of the bicameral parliaments in Australia). Omit if the stage was skipped (e.g. if no amendments were proposed or the chamber voted to skipped).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''conf_committee_passed'''
|In some jurisdictions, the date when the institution passed the version of the bill adopted by a [[conference committee]].
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading_for<br />1st_reading_for<br />2nd_reading_for<br />3rd_reading_for<br />passed_for<br />conf_committee_passed_for'''
|How many members voted for the bill in a given reading or other vote for passage.

Do not use this parameter if the vote is not taken on the bill as a whole (e.g. second readings in Israel).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading_against<br />1st_reading_against<br />2nd_reading_against<br />3rd_reading_against<br />passed_against<br />conf_committee_passed_against'''
|How many members voted against the bill in a given reading or other vote for passage.

Do not use this parameter if the vote is not taken on the bill as a whole (e.g. second readings in Israel).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading_abstention<br />1st_reading_abstention<br />2nd_reading_abstention<br />3rd_reading_abstention<br />passed_abstention<br />conf_committee_passed_abstention'''
|How many members voted to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote") in a given reading or other vote for passage.

Do not use this parameter if the vote is not taken on the bill as a whole (e.g. second readings in Israel).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading_absent<br />1st_reading_absent<br />2nd_reading_absent<br />3rd_reading_absent<br />passed_absent<br />conf_committee_passed_absent'''
|How many members were absent from the vote in a given reading or other vote for passage.

Do not use this parameter if the vote is not taken on the bill as a whole (e.g. second readings in Israel).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''preliminary_reading_presentnotvoting<br />1st_reading_presentnotvoting<br />2nd_reading_presentnotvoting<br />3rd_reading_presentnotvoting<br />passed_presentnotvoting<br />conf_committee_passed_presentnotvoting'''
|How many members were present at the vote in a given reading or other vote for passage, but did not vote. This does not include a vote to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote").

Do not use this parameter if the vote is not taken on the bill as a whole (e.g. second readings in Israel).
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''committee_report'''
|The name of a report issued by a legislative committee about the bill that was eventually enacted. If the report is available online, create an external link to it.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''bill2<br />bill_citation2<br />bill_date2<br />member_in_charge2<br />rapporteur2<br />introduced_on2<br />committee_responsible<br />preliminary_reading2<br />preliminary_reading2_for<br />preliminary_reading2_against<br />preliminary_reading2_abstention<br />preliminary_reading2_absent<br />preliminary_reading2_presentnotvoting<br />1st_reading2<br />1st_reading2_for<br />1st_reading2_against<br />1st_reading2_abstention<br />1st_reading2_absent<br />1st_reading2_presentnotvoting<br />committee_post1st2<br />2nd_reading2<br />2nd_reading2_for<br />2nd_reading2_against<br />2nd_reading2_abstention<br />2nd_reading2_absent<br />2nd_reading2_presentnotvoting<br />committee_post2nd2<br />committee_whole_label2<br />committee_whole2<br />3rd_reading2<br />3rd_reading2_for<br />3rd_reading2_against<br />3rd_reading2_abstention<br />3rd_reading2_absent<br />1st_reading2_presentnotvoting<br />passed2<br />passed2_for<br />passed2_against<br />passed2_abstention<br />passed2_absent<br />passed2_presentnotvoting<br />conf_committee_passed2<br />conf_committee_passed2_for<br />conf_committee_passed2_against<br />conf_committee_passed2_abstention<br />conf_committee_passed2_absent<br />conf_committee_passed2_presentnotvoting<br />committee_report2'''
|In a bicameral legislature, use these parameters to specify information about the bill that was considered in one chamber after it was passed by the other chamber.

In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, such as most Continental European legislatures, the <code>passed2</code>, <code>passed2_for</code>, <code>passed2_against</code>, <code>passed2_abstention</code>, <code>passed2_absent</code>, and <code>passed2_presentnotvoting</code> parameters apply to the decision of the second chamber to reject a bill, to pass it in an amended version, or (in the Czech Senate's case) to resolve not to consider the bill; if the second chamber didn't decide on the bill within the alloted time, <code>passed2</code> should be used to specify the date on which the time-limit ended.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_conf_committee'''
|In some jurisdictions, the date when a conference committee passed a bill. This parameter should be used together with {{para|conf_committee_passed}} and {{para|conf_committee_passed2}} – use these parameters to indicate the dates when the upper and lower legislative chambers passed the version of the bill adopted by the conference committee.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''second_chamber_action'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, the action taken by the second chamber on the bill. The possible values are:
*rejected
*passed after rejection
*passed with amendments
*amendments rejected
*resolved not to consider
*passed by inaction
If {{para|second_chamber_action}} is left empty, or if some value other than the ones above is given to, "Passed" is displayed.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_conf_committee'''
|In some jurisdictions, the date when a conference committee passed a bill. This parameter should be used together with {{para|conf_committee_passed}} and {{para|conf_committee_passed2}} – use these parameters to indicate the dates when the upper and lower legislative chambers passed the version of the bill adopted by the conference committee.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''white_paper'''
|The name of a [[white paper#Government white papers|white paper]] relating to the legislation. If the white paper is available online, create an external link to it.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_amendments_considered'''
|In bicameral legislatures, if amendments were made to the bill by the second chamber, the date(s) when these amendments were considered by the originating chamber. This includes a rejection of the bill in bicameral legislatures that employ an asymmetrical process.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amendments_considered_for'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, how many members voted for the first chamber's final decision on the amendments or rejection made by the second chamber.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amendments_considered_against'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, how many members voted against the first chamber's final decision on the amendments or rejection made by the second chamber.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amendments_considered_abstention'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, how many members voted to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote") in the first chamber's final decision on the amendments or rejection made by the second chamber.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amendments_considered_absent'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, how many members were absent from the vote in the first chamber's final decision on the amendments or rejection made by the second chamber.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amendments_considered_presentnotvoting'''
|In a bicameral legislature that employs an asymmetrical process, how many members were present at the vote in the first chamber's final decision on the amendments or rejection made by the second chamber, but did not vote. This does not include a vote to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote").
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_final_passage'''
|In bicameral legislatures that employ a symmetrical process, the date when all amendments to the bill have been ultimately considered and the bill has finally passed both chambers.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_reconsidered'''
|The date when a vetoed bill, returned to the legislature, was reconsidered by the institution specified in {{para|enacted_by}} or {{para|considered_by}}.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_override_for'''
|How many members voted for a veto override during the first chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_override_against'''
|How many members voted against a veto override during the first chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_override_abstention'''
|How many members voted to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote") in the first chamber's vote on a veto override during the first chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_override_absent'''
|How many members were absent from the first chamber's vote on a veto override during the first chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''veto_override_presentnotvoting'''
|How many members were present at the first chamber's vote on a veto override during the first chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill, but did not vote. This does not include a vote to abstain (however called in the jurisdiction; e.g. "present", "blank vote").
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''date_reconsidered2<br />veto_override2_for<br />veto_override2_against<br />veto_override2_abstention<br />veto_override2_absent<br />veto_override2_presentnotvoting'''
|In a bicameral legislature, use these parameters to specify information about the second chamber's reconsideration of a vetoed bill.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amends'''
|The citations of any notable legislation that this legislation amends. If available, wikilink the article or external link the texts of the amended legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''repeals'''
|The citations of any notable legislation that this legislation repeals. If available, wikilink the article or external link the texts of the repealed legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''amended_by'''
|The citations of any notable amendments to this legislation. If available, wikilink the article or external link the texts of the amendments.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''repealed_by'''
|The citations of any notable legislation repealing parts or previous versions of this legislation. If available, wikilink the article or external link the texts of the repealing legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''related_legislation'''
|The names and citations of any related pieces of legislation. Where possible, link the name of a related piece of legislation to a Wikipedia article about it, and link the citation to an external website containing the text of the related legislation.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''related_cases'''
|Court cases of the jurisdiction's supreme court relating to this legislation. Where possible, link the name of a court case to a Wikipedia article about it, and link the citation to an external website containing the text of the ruling.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''supreme_court'''
|Name of the supreme court issuing the cases listed in {{para|related_cases}}.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''struck_down_by'''
|The citations of any court case striking down this legislation as unconstitutional. Where possible, link the name of a court case to a Wikipedia article about it, and link the citation to an external website containing the text of the ruling.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''summary'''
|A very brief summary of the subjects that the legislation deals with.
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''keywords'''
|A list of [[:en:Index term|keywords]] that describe the legal issues dealt with by the legislation. List keywords alphabetically, separate them with commas, and link them to appropriate Wikipedia articles wherever possible; for example, "{{mono|<nowiki>[[Bailment]], [[common carrier]], [[negligence]], [[strict liability]]</nowiki>}}".
|-
|colspan="2" bgcolor="silver"|'''Status'''
|-
| style="text-align:center;" |'''status'''
|The status of the bill or legislation. The possible values are:
{|
|-
|
*pending
*pending first
*pending second
*pending referendum
*pending assent
*not passed
*vetoed
*veto override failed
*current
*not yet in force
*not fully in force
|
*halted
*in force
*amended
*expired
*repealed
*spent
*struck down
*disallowed
*abrogated
*void
*void ab initio
|}
If some value other than the ones above is given to {{para|status}}, "Unknown" is displayed.
|}

==Images==
The image parameter was unilaterally removed along with supporting parameters in November 2024 because it was generally used only to display decorative logos of the legislature that considered the law (which goes against [[:en:MOS:IMAGERELEVANCE|MOS:IMAGERELEVANCE]]); it was later restored as part of a [[WP:BOLD, revert, discuss cycle]] process.

In the rare cases where an image specifically illustrates the law in question, whether in its topic or in its enactment process (such as [[Enabling Act of 1933]]), or helps to differentiates between similar laws of different jurisdictions (such as [[:en:Australia Act 1986|Australia Act 1986]], where the coats of arms help tell the UK and Australian versions of the act from each other), the images in question can be displayed within the infobox.
